sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Mail-Order Retail with Cash on Delivery Settlement

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid - Civil Law (Civil Code of Quebec) for private law matters; Common Law for public law and criminal law at the federal level; federal common law overlay in commercial and constitutional matters
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: CETA (Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, provisionally applied since 2017)
CPTPP (Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership, effective for Canada 30 December 2018)
Canada-China Agreement for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (FIPA, in force 1 October 2014)
Canada-China Income Tax Agreement (1986) as amended by the 2013 Protocol

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c. 17, as amended, and associated FINTRAC Regulations; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c. C-46, s. 462.31 (money laundering offences); Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c. C-44, ss. 21.1-21.42 (Individuals with Significant Control for federal corporations); Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c. S-31.1, s. 13-14 (control information); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1 (Quebec enterprise register and declarations); Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c. 17; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c. U-2; Global Affairs Canada Consolidated Sanctions Regulations
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access - REQ accepts UBO and significant-control declarations; access is restricted to authorized regulators (FINTRAC, CRA, Revenu Quebec), law enforcement, and financial institutions conducting client due diligence with consent; not available for general public browsing

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Corporate Existence or Certificate of Incumbency of any non-resident corporate shareholder (emerging-market parent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille - issued by the home jurisdiction's competent authority (for PRC origin, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China); Canada acceded effective 11 January 2024

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized UBO Declaration and Source of Funds Certificate (attesting ultimate individual ownership and lawful origin of COD escrow capital)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Quebec notary (acte notarie) or home-country notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for Hague member origin; Consular Legalization for non-Hague origin; followed by certified French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy and proof of residential address of each Ultimate Beneficial Owner (25% or more) and of each director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country issuing authority (police, national registry) or notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus certified French translation per OTTIAQ standards

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and financial standing confirmation for the COD payment rails (Airwallex aggregator account and local logistics remittance settlement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed financial institution or money service business regulator in the emerging-market jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, if unregulated source, Consular Legalization at the competent consulate; certified French translation required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate of the designated director(s) and ultimate beneficial owner(s) (good conduct record)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police or Ministry of Public Security of the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (PRC: Ministry of Foreign Affairs apostille process) plus certified French translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against: FINTRAC guidance under PCMLTFA; Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions list (Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act); Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) notices; United Nations Security Council consolidated list; OFAC SDN list (because Airwallex USD and CAD settlement rails are exposed to US dollar clearing); Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) determination for foreign heads of state, ministers, senior officials, and their close associates; enhanced due diligence triggered by cash-on-delivery retail volume, cross-border remittance, and emerging-market beneficial owners; negative news, adverse media, and source-of-wealth verification must be documented and refreshed every 6 months.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - Registre des entreprises electronique, available at https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca (including online name reservation and DQ declaration portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, ss. 18-35 mandates that the corporate name be in French; a non-French name may be retained only with the authorization of the Office quebecois de la langue francaise and must appear together with a corresponding French form; transliteration into Latin script following French phonetic rules is required; an English trade name requires a descriptive French element; the REQ rejects any name consisting solely of numerals or symbols without a French language component.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Societe (when implying a regulated statutory form)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a REQ name refusal notice, the applicant must file a written administrative review with the Director of the Registraire des entreprises within 30 days under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, ss. 42-45, attaching the rejection notice, the originally proposed name, and any legal opinion on registrability; if the review is upheld, the applicant may appeal to the Administrative Tribunal of Quebec within 60 days; concurrently the applicant may submit an amended French-compliant name with a new name-certificate reservation; a refusal does not suspend the option to re-file with a corrected distinctive element within the original validity window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible for the registered office only if the service provider maintains a physical street address in Quebec capable of receiving statutory service of process and REQ/CRA correspondence; a registered office cannot be a post office box or a mere mail-forwarding node. For the cash-on-delivery retail business, a virtual office alone will not constitute commercial substance: CRA and Revenu Quebec require actual inventory custody, order processing, or contract management in Quebec, failing which the corporation risks non-recognition as an active Quebec business and diminished permanent establishment protection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months: medium-risk-enhanced AML classification for COD e-commerce, combined with non-resident UBOs and offshore remittance rails, triggers REQ verification visits and CRA GST/HST field audits; the probability rises to 55% if the UBO is flagged as PEP or if regulatory filings disclose inconsistencies.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation and clearance certificate (certificat de reservation) before the Registraire des entreprises
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff - REQ fee schedule published in the Gazette officielle du Quebec (CAD 40 for name certificate)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing of articles of incorporation under the Quebec Business Corporations Act (online filing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff - REQ online filing fee CAD 147 (approx. USD 108 at prevailing CAD/USD exchange rate)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial civil-law notarization of the articles of incorporation and UBO sworn declaration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Quebec notary (notaire) - Chambre des notaires du Quebec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark: CAD 200-400 notarial fee for incorporation act and UBO declaration depending on complexity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille of foreign corporate existence certificate and passport copies (per document set)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Global Affairs Canada Authentication Service or competent authority of the emerging-market origin state (for PRC origin: Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee CAD 30 per document at Global Affairs Canada; foreign competent authority fees vary by jurisdiction

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of apostilled UBO and corporate documents (per page bundle)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translator member of OTTIAQ (Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interpretes agrees du Quebec)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark CAD 45-90 per page under OTTIAQ recommended tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial enterprise registration and declaration (declaration de renseignements) - first annual period
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory annual registration tariff under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CAD 40 per year)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and domiciliation service - Quebec physical street address with service-of-process handling (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Corporate service provider licensed by the REQ
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark CAD 250-400 per year for registered office services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: External counsel pre-incorporation due diligence and filing package (AML, name clearance, UBO register, and compliance certificate)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Quebec business law firm (member of the Barreau du Quebec)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark fixed fee CAD 500-1,000 for pre-incorporation compliance package

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1, as amended, including the provisions governing incorporation, registered office, directors and officers; supplementary rules in the CQLR c S-31.1 r 1 (Company Fee and Form Regulation).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar / REQ)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the corporation may be incorporated without paid-up capital. Share considerations are fixed by directors and must be lawful; no escrow account is required at the incorporation stage.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation documents and articles of incorporation be confirmed; that the issuance of [number] common shares to the initial subscribers for lawful consideration be approved, and that share certificates be executed; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at the address stated in the articles and that the designated registrant be authorized to record this address with the Registraire des entreprises; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the following persons be appointed as officers: [individuals] as President, Secretary, and Treasurer, each to serve until replaced; and that the officers are authorized to open bank accounts and complete all filings required by law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — CLIC online name search and reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search and, if necessary, file a declaration of name through the REQ online portal. The proposed name must be distinctive and not contrary to public order. Retain the name search report for submission with the articles of incorporation. A reserved name is valid for 120 days.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report dated within 90 days
Consent letters from individuals whose names appear in the corporate name
Proposed corporate name and bilingual/English/French alternatives
Registered office street address for the name declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ rejects the name on distinctiveness grounds, amend the proposed name and resubmit; if the report is stale, obtain a refreshed NUANS report and refile.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — CLIC electronic incorporation filing window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the REQ articles of incorporation form, setting out the corporate name, share structure, number and class of shares, restrictions on share transfers, number of directors, and the registered office. Execute the articles with the incorporators and directors, pay the prescribed fee, and transmit the filing electronically or in paper form to the REQ. Upon acceptance, the REQ issues a certificate of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Completed articles of incorporation form
NUANS name search report
Consent to act as director forms for each director
Proof of payment of filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ issues a notice of intended refusal, correct the stated defects and resubmit; if the articles are accepted with errors, file supplementary articles or request annulment and re-incorporation within the applicable statutory period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Registered Office and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — online record update service; corporate records held at the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the registered office address in Quebec for service of process and corporate records retention. Maintain the registers of shareholders, directors, and officers, and the corporate seal, at the registered office. Record the corporate records book and update REQ with any subsequent address change through a notice of amendment.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation
Articles of incorporation
Notice of registered office or declaration of address
Corporate by-laws and initial meeting minutes
Shareholder and director registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ queries the address or records, provide a corrected declaration and proof of physical location in Quebec; cure any validation gap by filing a replacement notice of registered office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Initial Corporate Governance and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directors and shareholders acting through the corporate record; filings with the REQ as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting by written resolution. Adopt the corporate by-laws, approve share subscription, issue share certificates to the initial subscribers, appoint the officers, and authorize bank account opening and external filings. Execute the pro-forma board resolution and ensure that all statutory registers reflect the appointments.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first board resolution
Consent to act as directors and officers
Share subscription agreements and consideration records
Corporate by-laws
Initial share certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ or a financial institution rejects the appointment documentation, re-execute the resolution, obtain corrected consents, and file an updated notice of appointment or change of officers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, Revenu Québec, CNESST, and municipal licensing office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) and federal Business Number (BN), register for GST/QST accounts, apply for payroll deductions account, register with CNESST for workplace safety, and apply for any municipal business licence. Confirm that cash-on-delivery logistics and distribution activities, including warehouse occupancy, are covered by the municipal zoning and occupancy permits.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and articles
Registered office address confirmation
Director and officer government identification
Warehouse or commercial lease and occupancy authorization
Bank account confirmation for payment rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a tax account is queried or suspended, respond to the notice with corrected registration data; if municipal licensing is denied, remedy zoning or occupancy deficiencies and apply for a variance or equivalent permit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Economic Development and Permitting Department / local zoning and building safety office (Service de l'urbanisme et des permis)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificate of Occupancy (Certificat d'occupation) and Municipal Business Licence (Permis de commerce)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category A / Registration regime for mail-order retail distribution and warehousing; a full EIA study is not required unless the project involves significant storage of hazardous materials, groundwater discharge, or development in a sensitive zone. A declaration of compliance or registration may be required for wastewater and atmospheric emissions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Commercial wastewater discharges must comply with municipal sewer by-laws and applicable Quebec effluent standards, including limits on BOD, suspended solids, and prohibited substances; volatile organic compound emissions must meet provincial clean air regulation thresholds and be reported if the relevant mandatory reporting trigger is exceeded. Hazardous waste handling must comply with the Regulation respecting hazardous materials.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the competent municipal fire safety authority, structural load inspection and approval by a qualified engineer, CNESST workplace health and safety registration, and municipal clearance confirming compliance with fire code, building code, and occupational safety requirements for the warehouse and distribution premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Revenu Québec (RQ) for Quebec provincial taxes and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal taxes. Official portals: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/ and https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: To obtain statutory tax identification, Canadian corporations file for a Business Number (BN) with the CRA via the online portal or Form RC1. Quebec corporations register with Revenu Québec for the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ). Foreign entities establishing operations in Canada follow identical incorporation and registration steps.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or similar elections available for corporations. Entity-level taxation applies. Hybrid mismatch rules are addressed under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/QST (Goods and Services Tax / Quebec Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time electronic invoicing or clearance mandate exists. Invoices must meet statutory form requirements. Digital options are available but not compulsory.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada qualify for 0% GST/QST rate upon submission of export proof. Offshore services may be zero-rated if not consumed in Canada. For mail-order retail with cash on delivery, eligibility requires verified shipment and export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent export zero-rating claims result in audits, penalties of 200% of evaded tax, fines, and possible criminal prosecution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates under a floating exchange rate regime with unrestricted convertibility for current account transactions including trade settlements and services. Capital account transactions require prior approval from the Department of Finance under the Investment Canada Act for certain foreign investments. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are convertible without surrender but subject to 25% withholding tax on dividends. No capital controls apply to Canadian corporations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory mandatory surrender or forced conversion of export receipts. Receipts must be deposited into corporate accounts and may be utilized for operational purposes. Banks may request supporting documentation for large transactions; voluntary reporting to FINTRAC or Statistics Canada applies for AML and statistical purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High viability for fintech EMI providers such as Airwallex in cross-border COD remittances, subject to FINTRAC registration as a money services business, enhanced KYC/AML obligations under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, and compliance with the Payment Services Act. Offshore digital EMIs require local Canadian entity incorporation or licensed correspondent banking arrangements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not strictly mandated for all directors in routine KYC for established Canadian corporations; video conferencing or in-person interviews are often required depending on risk assessment and entity history. Remote account opening is permitted under FINTRAC guidelines with digital ID verification for low to medium risk profiles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership not disclosed or shell company indicators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation, articles of association, beneficial ownership register, source of funds proof

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions involving sanctioned jurisdictions or inconsistent ownership information
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Export contracts, shipping documents, payment proofs, updated beneficial ownership declaration, and corporate filings

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital via international wire transfers (SWIFT MT103) using purpose codes such as 'CAP' for capital contributions or 'EQTY' for equity. All transactions require supporting documentation including board resolutions, shareholder agreements, and proof of non-resident status where applicable. Verification through correspondent banking channels and compliance with the Investment Canada Act for foreign direct investment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements facilitated through SWIFT MT103 for remittances or Commercial Letters of Credit (LCs) governed by UCP 600. For cash-on-delivery ecommerce, integration with local logistics partners for remittance collection and settlement. Purpose codes must reflect trade nature to avoid AML flags.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days of the anniversary of incorporation or the filing date of the prior return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to $500 CAD; administrative dissolution possible if filings remain outstanding for two consecutive years

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit required for distributing corporations; for non-distributing corporations, audit required only if stipulated in articles of incorporation or requested by shareholders
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) or Canadian GAAP

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No mandatory annual beneficial ownership confirmation; shareholders must notify and update shareholding and UBO information upon any material change

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% (15% federal general rate + 11.5% Quebec general corporate rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal Small Business Deduction reduces federal active business income tax to 9% on the first C$500,000; Quebec applies a reduced SME rate of 3.2%, resulting in a combined preferential rate of 12.2%. No statutory holiday is specific to mail-order retail, cash-on-delivery settlement, or the declared ISIC 4791 activity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return – Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) via NETFILE/EFILE authorized software or CRA My Business Account
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due no later than 6 months after the fiscal year-end; balance-of-tax payment is due 2 months after the fiscal year-end for Canadian-controlled private corporations, with different schedules for other corporations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal corporate name, business number, jurisdiction of incorporation, registered office address, and fiscal period end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Canadian branch or permanent establishment fiscal period end and indicate the treaty-residency country; complete the non-resident identification schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate worldwide revenue separated by Canadian-source and foreign-source business income, including mail-order retail sales, C.O.D. delivery surcharges, and ancillary logistics fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident corporation, report only income reasonably attributable to the Canadian permanent establishment under section 115 of the Income Tax Act and the applicable tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses, excluding unsubstantiated costs; include cost of goods shipped, freight, payment-processing fees, and estimated bad debt from refused C.O.D. parcels.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions must be directly incurred to earn Canadian-source income; head-office and cross-border overhead expenses must be allocated in compliance with provincial allocation and treaty provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation after application of non-capital loss carryforwards, capital loss restrictions, and business income adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply loss carryforward only against Canadian-source taxable income; respect the 20-year non-capital loss carryforward period and any deemed-year-end rules for ceased Canadian operations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing penalty under ITA s.162(1): 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month of delinquency up to 12 months; repeat failure attracts 10% plus 2% per month. Arrears interest accrues daily. A separate penalty for failure to provide required information may apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return – Revenu Québec via the CLICK netfile system
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 6 months after the fiscal year-end, consistent with federal T2 filing; provincial instalment payments follow the Quebec Taxation Act instalment calendar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec registration number, business name, enterprise number, fiscal year, and status under the Quebec Business Corporations Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations with a Quebec permanent establishment must register with Revenu Québec and report that establishment; attach treaty allocation schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue and gross profit from all business activities carried on in Quebec, including C.O.D. retail sales booked through Canadian or foreign payment processors.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Quebec-attributable business revenue and exclude income allocated to other jurisdictions in accordance with the Quebec allocation and treaty rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction for non-capital loss carryforwards, tax credits, and the provincial small business deduction calculation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may claim Quebec loss carryforward only if the income was subject to Quebec tax in the relevant year; attach the loss carryforward schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of Quebec income tax payable after non-refundable tax credits, refundable credits, and minimum tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Quebec minimum tax and dividend allocation rules; non-residents must remit Quebec withholding on distributions to non-residents.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Revenu Québec imposes a late-filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months; repeat failures attract 10% plus 2% per month. Provincial interest is compounded on arrears and a third-party informant penalty may also apply.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% federal Part XIII statutory rate; Quebec imposes an additional 12% non-resident dividend tax under section 1091 of the Taxation Act, for a combined statutory gross rate of 37% absent treaty relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident recipient must submit CRA Form NR301 (Application for Treaty-Based Relief) to the Canadian payer before payment, provide a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the residence-country tax authority, and where required complete NR302/NR303 identification disclosure. Revenu Québec recognizes federal treaty reductions and will cap the aggregate federal and Quebec withholding at the applicable DTA rate. The payer should retain the TRC, certified ownership chain documentation, and a completed NR301 in the corporate books.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 25% federal Part XIII statutory, plus 12% Quebec where applicable; typical DTA reduction to 10% for industrial/copyright royalties. Interest: 25% federal Part XIII statutory, but arm's-length interest generally benefits from the s.212(3)(b) exemption, and most Canadian DTAs reduce total withholding to 0%; non-arm's-length related-party interest remains subject to statutory 25% absent treaty and domestic exemption conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No fixed statutory Local File threshold exists; CRA expects contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation for all non-arm's-length cross-border transactions, including logistics fees, payment-processing charges, and intercompany inventory transfers. Country-by-Country Report and Master File are mandatory for multinational groups with consolidated annual revenue equal to or greater than C$1 billion; mid-market groups should maintain a Local File in all material related-party transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not maintain a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime of the type seen in offshore financial centres. Instead, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (ITA s.245) and the Quebec GAAR deny tax benefits arising from artificial or sham transactions. A C.O.D. e-commerce operation must demonstrate a tangible Canadian footprint – inventory carriage, physical logistics contracts, operational personnel, and substantive order management – otherwise tax authorities may recharacterize the whole structure as a sham.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately failing to record cash-on-delivery transactions, maintaining parallel off-book ledgers, depositing cash proceeds into personal accounts of directors or related non-resident entities, and omitting such income from the T2 and CO-17 returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under ITA s.239: fines of 50% to 200% of the evaded federal tax plus imprisonment for up to 5 years; Quebec Tax Administration Act adds separate fines of up to C$1,000,000 for provincial tax evasion. Reassessments may add penalties of up to 50% of the tax evaded plus compounded arrears interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participated in underreporting are jointly and severally liable under ITA s.227.1 for withheld amounts and tax liabilities. On indictment, travel bans and bail conditions may be imposed; civil restitution and asset freezes are available to the tax authorities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unreasonable Transfer Pricing Resulting in Base Erosion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging excessive intercompany logistics, commission, or payment-processing fees to a related offshore entity without showing an arm's-length pricing analysis; failure to keep contemporaneous Local File documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: TP reassessment under ITA s.247(2) and Quebec equivalent; a penalty of 10% of the net transfer-pricing adjustment is imposed if the taxpayer did not make reasonable documentation efforts and the adjustment exceeds the prescribed threshold. Deductibility is denied and interest runs from the applicable reassessment period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or sign false documentation can lose statutory reliance protection and be assessed for negligence and failure-to-withhold amounts. In fraud cases, directors may face criminal charges and civil liability for resulting unpaid taxes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Canadian corporation with only a registered agent, no physical fulfilment, no employees, no integral logistics function, and directing all C.O.D. revenue through a related foreign shell while claiming Canadian treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment under ITA s.245 (and Quebec GAAR) with a 25% penalty on the tax benefit; penalties for foreign reporting in Part XVIII (T1134/T1135) of up to C$2,500 per failure and C$25,000 per gross negligence misrepresentation may apply. Criminal money-laundering charges under the Criminal Code are available if funds are routed through sham structures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil where the corporation is a mere facade, exposing directors to personal liability for unpaid taxes and civil restitution. Travel bans and terrorism/AML asset freezing orders are possible when cross-border shell transactions are coupled with cash layering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Ignoring mandatory cash transaction disclosure for C.O.D. sales with single or related cash receipts exceeding C$10,000, failing to maintain beneficial ownership records, structuring cash flows below thresholds, or using unregistered payment intermediaries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, up to C$500,000 for the first violation and up to C$1,000,000 for repeat violations; criminal penalties can include imprisonment of up to 5 years and fines up to C$2,000,000 for violating AML obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly fail to implement AML controls can be prosecuted as principals or accessories, face personal administrative fines, and be prohibited from acting as directors under Canadian corporate law. Travel bans and asset seizure may be ordered in connection with laundering charges.
